summary: Walter Porzig was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Jena (~1913–1920) and under Wilhelm Streitberg (~1920–1921). He held academic posts at Leipzig, Bern, Jena (~1936–1945), and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (~1951–1961).
Walter Ruben was an Indologist. He held academic positions at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1931–1935), the University of Chile (~1948–1950), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1950–1965).

Walter Simon specialized in Sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Otto Franke and August Hermann Francke, later holding posts at Berlin, Kiel, the National Library of China, and the University of London (1938–1960).

Walter Slaje is an Indologist who completed his Promotion and Habilitation at the University of Vienna. He worked at Graz University Library (1984–1995) and served as director at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1995–2020).

Walter William Skeat was a scholar in linguistics. He studied at Highgate School, King's College School, and the University of Cambridge (Christ's College), where he later held an academic post from around 1878 to 1912.

Walther Heissig worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies as well as religious studies. He studied at Vienna, Humboldt University, Göttingen, and Bonn, and held posts at Peking University, Fu Jen Catholic University, and the University of Bonn.

Walther Schubring was an Indologist who studied at Munich and Strasbourg, where he completed a doctorate under Ernst Leumann. He worked at the Prussian State Library (1907) and held the Indology chair at the University of Hamburg (1920–1951).

Walther Wüst was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Munich (1920–1923). He served as dean at Munich (1935–1945), department head at the Ahnenerbe (1936), and president of the Deutsche Akademie (1943).

Wannaporn Rienjang is an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD from the University of Cambridge. She held positions at the British Museum, the Classical Art Research Centre (attested 2019–2022), and Thammasat University (attested 2022–2023).

Warren Cowgill was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Stanford University (~1948–1952) and completed his PhD at Yale University (~1952–1957), where he became a professor of linguistics in 1956.
Warren Lee Todd is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who earned his PhD at Lancaster University under the supervision of Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad (attested 2012).

Warrin Ratanamalai is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, where he studied under supervisors Phra Suthithammanuwat and Phra Srisitthimuni, as well as teachers Phra Sudhivorayan and Phramaha Somjin Sammāpañño.

Watari Yanai was a scholar in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1899–1903) and subsequently held an academic post there from around 1908 to 1926.

Wataru Mori studied at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1951). He worked in the fields of philosophy and other subjects, holding posts at Tokyo Medical and Dental University (~1966–1973) and the University of Tokyo (~1973–1989).

Wataru S. Ryose is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1987 under the doctoral supervision of Minoru Kiyota, having also studied under Genjun Sasaki and Frances A. Wilson.

Wayne Proudfoot is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Harvard Divinity School and Harvard University (PhD ~1972). He held academic posts at Fordham University (~1970–1972) and Columbia University (~1972–2008).

Wei Lin, a scholar of archaeology and Buddhist studies, studied at Nanjing University, Peking University, and Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. Her career includes posts at Nanjing Municipal Museum and Transylvania University (attested 2007).
Wei Pachow is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He studied under Tan Yun-shan and served on the teaching and research staff at Visva-Bharati University.

Wei-Cheng Lin works in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill until 2015, when he took up a post at the University of Chicago.

Weijen Teng specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Chicago and Harvard University under supervisors Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil, and joined the faculty at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts.
